specs.title: Production Scheduling (AHC flowshop)
specs.objective: minimize makespan
specs.io: jobs×machines times → schedule
specs.innovation: **NEH construction + critical-path-guided neighborhood** (only swap operations on the critical path change makespan) → O(1)-ish moves
specs.scoring: simulate schedule, output makespan

specs.title: Maze Treasure Collection (time-budgeted)
specs.objective: maximize collected value within T steps
specs.io: grid + values → move string
specs.innovation: **beam search over (position, collected-mask-summary) with a distance-to-value admissible heuristic** for pruning
specs.scoring: replay moves, sum value, check ≤T

specs.title: Cable Layout (rectilinear Steiner-ish)
specs.objective: minimize total wire length connecting terminals
specs.io: terminals → routing
specs.innovation: **Hanan-grid restriction + minimum-spanning-tree on Steiner candidates, then local rerouting**; the Hanan-grid relaxation cuts the search space
specs.scoring: sum routed length, verify connectivity

specs.title: Dynamic Bin Packing with Rebalancing
specs.objective: minimize #bins / overflow over a stream
specs.io: item stream → assignments
specs.innovation: **best-fit-decreasing online + periodic "repack the fullest few bins" move** with incremental fill tracking
specs.scoring: replay assignments, count bins/overflow

specs.title: Tiling-Color SA (AHC "wall painting")
specs.objective: maximize matched target pattern
specs.io: target grid + ops budget → op sequence
specs.innovation: **SA where the move = a single brush stroke and the score delta is computed only over the stroke's footprint** (O(stroke), not O(grid))
specs.scoring: apply ops to blank grid, count matches

specs.title: Vehicle Dispatch (assignment over time)
specs.objective: maximize fulfilled rides
specs.io: timed requests + vehicles → dispatch
specs.innovation: **rolling-horizon Hungarian on a small window + greedy carry-over**; the horizon relaxation makes a global NP problem tractable
specs.scoring: simulate dispatch, count fulfilled

specs.title: Lattice Antenna Coverage
specs.objective: maximize covered demand under power budget
specs.io: demand grid, budget → antenna set
specs.innovation: **greedy submodular-maximization (lazy-greedy / CELF) with marginal-gain caching**; lazy evaluation skips recomputing stale gains
specs.scoring: recompute coverage from output

specs.title: String Reassembly (shortest superstring approx)
specs.objective: minimize superstring length covering all fragments
specs.io: fragments → superstring
specs.innovation: **greedy max-overlap merge (Aho-Corisick overlaps) then 3-opt-style fragment reordering**; overlap graph relaxation of an NP problem
specs.scoring: verify all fragments are substrings; report length

specs.title: Graph Coloring with Soft Conflicts
specs.objective: minimize weighted conflict edges with ≤k colors
specs.io: graph, k → coloring
specs.innovation: **tabu search (TabuCol) with an incremental conflict-count table** updated in O(degree) per recolor; tabu tenure tuned to escape plateaus
specs.scoring: recount conflicts from output coloring

specs.title: Continuous Facility Layout (annealing on geometry)
specs.objective: minimize overlap + dispersion energy
specs.io: rectangles → positions
specs.innovation: **SA with a force-directed move proposal + spatial hash for O(1) neighbor overlap queries**; spatial hashing makes each move's delta cheap
specs.scoring: recompute energy from positions

specs.title: Prize-Collecting TSP (skip-the-loser tour)
specs.objective: maximize Σ(prize of visited nodes) − travel cost, with the option to skip nodes whose prize < detour cost
specs.io: `n`, depot, then `n` lines `x y prize` → first line `k`, then a permutation of `k` chosen node ids (a closed tour from depot)
specs.innovation: **Or-opt + node-insertion/removal hybrid: a single neighborhood that simultaneously (a) reorders the visited set and (b) toggles a node in/out, with an O(1) gain test = prize − (insert-detour) using cached prev/next pointers**; the in/out toggle is the non-obvious move competitors miss when they fix the visited set first
specs.scoring: scorer replays tour from depot, sums Euclidean travel + visited prizes, checks each id once and tour closed; profit = prizes − dist. Floor 0 if a repeated/illegal id or open tour. Normalize vs "visit-all nearest-neighbor tour"

specs.title: Capacitated Multi-Vehicle Routing
specs.objective: minimize total distance of `K` vehicle routes from a depot, each route's demand ≤ capacity `Q`, every customer served exactly once
specs.io: `n K Q`, depot, then `n` lines `x y demand` → `K` lines, each a list of customer ids (route)
specs.innovation: **sweep-construct then cross-route relocate/2-opt\*, where the move legality (capacity) is checked in O(1) from per-route load prefix sums and the distance delta touches only 4 edges**; the cross-route 2-opt\* (swap tail segments between two routes) is the move that fixes badly-balanced sweeps
specs.scoring: scorer sums all route distances (each route closed at depot), verifies every customer once and every route load ≤ Q. Floor 0 on overload/missing/duplicate. Normalize vs Clarke-Wright savings baseline

specs.title: TSP with Time Windows (soft lateness)
specs.objective: minimize travel distance + λ·(total lateness) over a single tour visiting all `n` nodes, each node openable only in `[e_i, l_i]` (early arrival waits, free; late arrival penalized)
specs.io: `n λ`, depot, then `n` lines `x y e l` → a permutation of `n` ids
specs.innovation: **forward time-propagation cache: store cumulative arrival time along the tour so an Or-opt segment move recomputes lateness only from the move point onward, and prune moves whose pre-move-point delta already worsens distance by > best**; treating "waiting" as free reshapes the cost landscape (the non-obvious part is the partial-recompute window)
specs.scoring: scorer simulates the tour: arrival = max(prev_departure + dist, e_i), lateness = max(0, arrival − l_i). Cost = dist + λ·Σlateness. Floor 0 if not a permutation. Normalize vs earliest-deadline-first ordering

specs.title: 2D Rectangle Strip Packing
specs.objective: minimize the height used to pack `n` axis-aligned rectangles (no rotation unless flagged) into a fixed-width `W` strip without overlap
specs.io: `n W`, then `n` lines `w h` → `n` lines `x y` (bottom-left corner of each rect, in input order)
specs.innovation: **skyline (bottom-left) placement driven by a permutation + per-rect rotate bit, optimized by SA over the permutation; the skyline gives an O(n) place-and-score and an O(1) "lowest feasible y at this x-span" via a segment max over the skyline array** — the skyline data structure is the innovation that makes each candidate cheap
specs.scoring: scorer reads corners, checks all rects in-strip and pairwise non-overlapping, reports max top edge (height). Floor 0 on any overlap/out-of-strip. Normalize vs first-fit-decreasing-height shelf packing

specs.title: Polyomino Tiling Coverage
specs.objective: maximize covered cells of an `H×W` board using a multiset of polyomino pieces (each piece usable ≤ given count, 4 rotations, no overlap)
specs.io: `H W P`, then for each of `P` piece types: cell count then offsets, then `avail` → list of placements `type rot r c`
specs.innovation: **row-bitmask collision test (each row of the board a 64-bit word, each placed piece precomputed as row-masks) + SA whose move adds/removes one placement with an incremental covered-count delta = popcount of the piece's footprint**; bitmask footprints make the legality+delta O(rows-of-piece)
specs.scoring: scorer applies placements, verifies counts/rotations/no-overlap/in-bounds, reports covered cells. Floor 0 on overlap or over-use of a piece. Normalize vs greedy largest-piece-first fill

specs.title: Guillotine Cutting Stock
specs.objective: minimize wasted area when cutting requested rectangles from fixed `W×H` sheets using only guillotine (edge-to-edge) cuts; multiple sheets allowed
specs.io: `n W H`, then `n` lines `w h` → for each placed rect: `sheet x y rot`; unplaced allowed but penalized
specs.innovation: **represent each sheet as a guillotine k-d tree of free rectangles; placement = best-fit leaf + split, and the SA move re-orders the insertion sequence (the tree is rebuilt by replay), exploiting that guillotine feasibility is automatic by construction** — encoding feasibility into the construction is the trick
specs.scoring: scorer replays insertions, verifies guillotine-legal non-overlapping placement within sheets; objective = Σ(area of unplaced)·penalty + Σ(used-sheet area − placed area). Floor 0 if any overlap/out-of-sheet. Normalize vs shelf-based next-fit

specs.title: Job-Shop Scheduling (makespan)
specs.objective: minimize makespan: `n` jobs each a fixed sequence of `m` operations on specified machines with given durations; a machine runs one op at a time
specs.io: `n m`, then `n` lines each `m` pairs `machine dur` → for each machine, the order of (job,op) it runs
specs.innovation: **disjunctive-graph model: a candidate is a machine-order; decode to start times by longest-path; the neighborhood swaps only adjacent ops on the *critical path* (a swap off the critical path can't reduce makespan), found by one backward pass** — restricting moves to the critical block is the established but non-obvious key
specs.scoring: scorer builds the schedule from the machine orders, checks job-precedence and machine-exclusivity, reports makespan (max completion). Floor 0 on any precedence/overlap violation. Normalize vs shortest-processing-time dispatch

specs.title: RCPSP (resource-constrained project scheduling)
specs.objective: minimize project completion time scheduling `n` tasks with precedence and `R` renewable resources of fixed capacity, each task consuming a fixed amount while running
specs.io: `n R`, capacities, then per task: dur, resource demands, predecessors → a start time per task
specs.innovation: **serial schedule-generation scheme driven by a priority list; the SA move = swap two tasks in the priority list (respecting precedence), and the resource feasibility at each insertion is tested with a per-resource time-profile array updated incrementally** — the priority-list encoding guarantees precedence-feasibility for free
specs.scoring: scorer decodes the priority list with the SGS, or directly validates given start times: checks precedence and that at every time no resource exceeds capacity; reports makespan. Floor 0 on infeasibility. Normalize vs earliest-start-time list

specs.title: Machine Assignment with Sequence-Dependent Setups
specs.objective: minimize total completion + setup time assigning `n` jobs to `M` parallel machines, where consecutive jobs on a machine incur a setup cost from a `type×type` matrix
specs.io: `n M T`, job types & durations, `T×T` setup matrix → per machine an ordered job list
specs.innovation: **two coupled neighborhoods: inter-machine move (relocate a job, delta touches setups of 2 donor + 2 receiver neighbors) and intra-machine 2-opt on the type-sequence; both deltas O(1) from cached neighbor types** — recognizing setup cost is a "TSP-on-types per machine" inside an assignment is the insight
specs.scoring: scorer sums per-machine (Σdur + Σ consecutive-setup), reports the makespan (max machine load) or total, per stated objective. Floor 0 if a job is unassigned/duplicated. Normalize vs balanced round-robin assignment

specs.title: Interval Scheduling on Few Rooms
specs.objective: maximize total weight of accepted intervals assigned to `K` identical rooms such that intervals in a room never overlap
specs.io: `n K`, then `n` lines `start end weight` → for each accepted interval, its room id (or −1 to reject)
specs.innovation: **greedy-by-weight with a per-room "earliest free time" min-heap gives a strong start; then SA swaps a rejected high-weight interval for a conflicting accepted one, with feasibility re-checked only inside the affected room via a balanced set of intervals** — the room-as-resource relaxation plus the targeted ejection move is the lever
specs.scoring: scorer verifies no two same-room intervals overlap; objective = Σ accepted weight. Floor 0 if a room has overlapping intervals. Normalize vs first-fit by start time

specs.title: Soft-Constraint Assignment (generalized)
specs.objective: maximize Σ preference scores assigning `n` agents to `m` slots (capacity per slot), minus penalties for violated soft constraints (e.g. "A and B should differ")
specs.io: `n m`, capacities, `n×m` preference matrix, soft-constraint list → a slot per agent
specs.innovation: **start from the LP/Hungarian-relaxation rounding (ignore soft constraints), then local search swapping two agents' slots with an O(1) penalty delta computed over only the constraints incident to the two moved agents** (constraint→agent incidence lists make the delta cheap)
specs.scoring: scorer checks capacities, sums preferences, subtracts soft-violation penalties. Floor 0 on capacity overflow. Normalize vs greedy-best-preference assignment

specs.title: Grid Light Placement (full coverage, min count)
specs.objective: minimize the number of placed lights on a grid so every floor cell is lit, where a light illuminates its row/column until blocked by a wall
specs.io: `H W`, grid of `.`/`#`, → list of light positions `r c`
specs.innovation: **model lit-segments as a set-cover over maximal horizontal+vertical corridors; greedy max-coverage seeds a solution, then SA removes a light and repairs any newly-dark cell with the cheapest covering candidate, using per-cell "covered-by-count" so removal feasibility is O(affected cells)** — the corridor decomposition turns a grid problem into set cover
specs.scoring: scorer simulates illumination (cast from each light until a wall), checks every floor cell lit, reports #lights. Floor 0 if any floor cell dark or a light on a wall. Normalize vs one-light-per-corridor baseline

specs.title: Sensor Placement for Coverage + Connectivity
specs.objective: maximize covered demand cells minus a connectivity penalty, placing `k` sensors (radius `r`) on a grid such that sensors form one connected component (adjacency within `2r`)
specs.io: `H W k r`, demand grid → `k` positions `r c`
specs.innovation: **lazy-greedy (CELF) submodular coverage for the placement, then a Steiner-style repair that nudges sensors to connect components along a min-spanning path; marginal coverage gains cached, recomputed only when invalidated** — combining submodular coverage with a connectivity repair is the non-obvious composition
specs.scoring: scorer computes covered demand (union of disks) and checks the connectivity graph is one component; objective = covered − λ·(#components−1). Floor 0 if more than `k` sensors. Normalize vs grid-spaced placement

specs.title: Connected Region Selection (max-weight connected subgrid)
specs.objective: maximize Σ cell weights of a chosen connected (4-adjacency) set of grid cells whose size ≤ budget `B`
specs.io: `H W B`, weight grid (may be negative) → list of chosen cells
specs.innovation: **seed at the best cell, grow via a priority frontier (best marginal cell), then SA that swaps a boundary cell out / a frontier cell in while maintaining connectivity via an incremental articulation-point check on the boundary only** — keeping connectivity under local moves cheaply (boundary-only bridge test) is the trick
specs.scoring: scorer checks the cells form one 4-connected component of size ≤ B, sums weights. Floor 0 if disconnected or over budget. Normalize vs greedy best-first growth

specs.title: Tower Placement for Signal (min towers, demand met)
specs.objective: minimize tower count so every demand node receives ≥ its required signal, where a tower at a site covers nearby demands with distance-decayed power
specs.io: `n m`, demand requirements, site→demand power matrix → chosen site subset
specs.innovation: **LP-relaxation of the covering ILP gives fractional site values; round greedily by "coverage-per-cost" and repair shortfalls by adding the site with max remaining-deficit gain (lazy-greedy), tracking each demand's accumulated signal in an array** — the fractional-relax-then-deterministic-round pipeline is the innovation
specs.scoring: scorer sums received signal per demand, checks all ≥ requirement, reports #towers. Floor 0 if any demand unmet. Normalize vs greedy max-coverage

specs.title: Balanced Districting (partition into K compact parts)
specs.objective: partition `n` weighted grid cells into `K` connected districts minimizing population imbalance + boundary length
specs.io: `H W K`, population grid → a district id per cell
specs.innovation: **multi-source BFS seeding for connected balanced starts, then a boundary-flip SA: move a border cell to a neighboring district, with an O(1) imbalance delta and an incremental connectivity guard (only the donor district can split, checked via local bridge test)** — the boundary-flip move with a donor-only split check keeps districts connected cheaply
specs.scoring: scorer checks each district is one 4-connected region, computes imbalance = Σ

specs.title: k-Means-Style Clustering with Cardinality Caps
specs.objective: minimize Σ point-to-assigned-center squared distance assigning `n` points to `k` centers with a per-cluster size cap
specs.io: `n k cap`, then `n` points → a center index per point + the `k` center coordinates
specs.innovation: **alternate (i) center = centroid of its members (closed form) and (ii) a capacitated assignment solved as a min-cost-flow / auction on the point→center cost, warm-started from the previous assignment so each round is near-incremental** — the capacity cap turns naive Lloyd into a transportation problem, the non-obvious reformulation
specs.scoring: scorer recomputes centroids from the assignment, sums squared distances, checks each cluster ≤ cap. Floor 0 if a cap is exceeded. Normalize vs uncapped Lloyd then greedy cap-repair

specs.title: Grid Wire Routing (min total length, no crossings)
specs.objective: minimize total wire length connecting `n` terminal pairs by monotone rectilinear paths on a grid such that no two wires share a cell
specs.io: `H W n`, then `n` lines `r1 c1 r2 c2` → for each pair, its path as a cell list
specs.innovation: **rip-up-and-reroute: route pairs one by one with A\* on a grid whose cost includes a congestion penalty for already-used cells; when a pair can't route, rip up the cheapest blocking wire and retry, raising its penalty (negotiated congestion)** — negotiated-congestion rerouting is the established but non-obvious heuristic from VLSI
specs.scoring: scorer checks each path connects its endpoints with unit steps and no cell used twice across wires; objective = Σ path lengths. Floor 0 on any shared cell or broken path. Normalize vs independent shortest paths (ignoring conflicts, counting conflicts as failures)

specs.title: Maze Carving to a Target Difficulty
specs.objective: maximize the shortest-path length from entrance to exit of a carved maze on an `H×W` grid, carving exactly `B` wall cells into corridor
specs.io: `H W B`, start/end, initial walls → list of `B` cells to carve open
specs.innovation: **treat it as a longest-induced-path-ish objective; greedily carve along a BFS tree that maximizes detour, then SA that swaps one carved cell for a neighbor, recomputing shortest path only if the swap touches the current shortest-path corridor (incremental BFS from the affected frontier)** — the "only recompute if the move intersects the current geodesic" pruning is the innovation
specs.scoring: scorer carves the chosen cells, runs BFS start→end, reports the shortest-path length (0 if unreachable). Floor 0 if not exactly `B` carved or start/end blocked. Normalize vs straight-corridor carve

specs.title: Flood-Control Levee Placement
specs.objective: minimize flooded cell count by placing `B` unit levees on a grid where water floods from source cells to all 4-connected lower-or-equal-height cells, levees blocking flow
specs.io: `H W B`, height grid, source cells → `B` levee cells
specs.innovation: **simulate flooding as a multi-source BFS over a "flow graph"; a levee deletes edges, so evaluate a levee set by BFS, and use a min-cut intuition — place levees on the current flood frontier's narrowest bottleneck, found via an edge-betweenness-like count from one flood pass** — using a single flood pass to score every candidate levee's marginal benefit is the trick
specs.scoring: scorer places levees, runs the flood simulation, counts flooded non-levee cells. Floor 0 if more than `B` levees. Normalize vs no-levee flood / random levees

specs.title: Sequencing to Minimize Weighted Tardiness
specs.objective: minimize Σ wᵢ·max(0, Cᵢ − dᵢ) sequencing `n` jobs on one machine (Cᵢ = completion time in the chosen order)
specs.io: `n`, then `n` lines `proc weight due` → a permutation of job ids
specs.innovation: **ATC (apparent tardiness cost) dispatch rule for the start, then a block-insertion neighborhood where moving a job changes completion times of an interval, recomputed in O(block) with a prefix-sum of processing times; prune by the EDD/SPT dominance conditions** — the dominance-pruned insertion neighborhood is the lever over naive swap
specs.scoring: scorer computes completion times along the order, sums weighted tardiness. Floor 0 if not a permutation. Normalize vs earliest-due-date order

specs.title: Permutation Flow Cost (quadratic objective)
specs.objective: minimize a quadratic arrangement cost Σ_{i<j} flow[a][b]·dist(pos_i,pos_j) — a QAP-style placement of `n` facilities on `n` locations
specs.io: `n`, flow matrix, distance matrix → a permutation (facility→location)
specs.innovation: **2-swap neighborhood with the standard QAP O(n) swap-delta formula (only rows/cols of the two swapped facilities change), plus a "don't-look bits" + tabu to escape the deep local minima QAP is infamous for** — the closed-form swap delta is what makes thousands of moves/sec feasible
specs.scoring: scorer reads the permutation, computes the full quadratic cost. Floor 0 if not a permutation. Normalize vs identity / a random-restart hill-climb baseline

specs.title: Continuous Point Placement then Snap
specs.objective: minimize a dispersion+coverage energy placing `k` points in `[0,L]²` to be spread out yet near demand, with the final answer snapped to integer grid coordinates
specs.io: `k L`, demand points → `k` integer coordinates
specs.innovation: **optimize in the continuous domain with gradient-like Lloyd/repulsion updates (centroidal-Voronoi relaxation), then snap each point to the best of its 4 surrounding integer cells chosen by a tiny local search on the discretized energy** — solving continuously then doing a structured integer-snap (not naive rounding) is the innovation
specs.scoring: scorer reads integer coordinates, computes the energy (e.g. Σ demand→nearest-point dist − λ·Σ min pairwise dist). Floor 0 if a coordinate is out of range. Normalize vs uniform-grid placement

specs.title: Parameter Placement for a Simulated Controller
specs.objective: maximize a simulated reward by choosing `p` real parameters (PID-like gains) that drive a deterministic dynamical simulation, parameters then quantized to a fixed grid
specs.io: `p`, sim spec (target trajectory, steps) → `p` quantized parameter values
specs.innovation: **coordinate-descent / Nelder-Mead in continuous space using the cheap forward simulation as the oracle, then refine on the quantized lattice; cache the simulation's per-step state so a single-parameter change re-runs only from the first divergent step** — treating the simulator as a black box but caching its prefix state is the efficiency trick
specs.scoring: scorer runs the frozen simulation with the quantized parameters and returns the reward (e.g. −Σ tracking error). Floor 0 if a parameter is out of bounds or the sim diverges (NaN/overflow). Normalize vs default zero-gain parameters

specs.title: Simulated Epidemic Containment (control loop)
specs.objective: minimize total infections over `T` days by choosing, each day, which of `n` regions to lock down under a daily budget of `b` lockdowns; spread is a deterministic SIR-on-a-graph
specs.io: `n T b`, region graph, initial infections, SIR rates → a `T×?` schedule of locked region ids per day
specs.innovation: **rolling-horizon greedy: at each day pick the `b` regions with the highest projected forward-infection contribution estimated by a short k-step simulation lookahead, with the lookahead reusing the cached current state**; the look-ahead marginal-infection score is the non-obvious control signal
specs.scoring: scorer runs the full deterministic SIR simulation applying the schedule, reports total cumulative infections (objective minimize). Floor 0 if any day exceeds `b` lockdowns. Normalize vs lock-the-most-infected-today greedy

specs.title: Online Bin Assignment (sequential, partial info)
specs.objective: maximize packed value assigning each arriving item (revealed one at a time) to one of `K` bins of fixed capacity, decisions irrevocable, future items unknown until they arrive
specs.io: interactive/streamed: `K`, capacities, then items one per line `size value` until EOF → one bin id per item as it arrives
specs.innovation: **threshold/secretary-style online policy: maintain per-bin remaining capacity and accept an item into the bin maximizing value-density only if its value exceeds an adaptive threshold tuned from the empirical value distribution seen so far** — the adaptive acceptance threshold under partial info is the heuristic-design core
specs.scoring: local scorer replays the stream feeding the solver one item at a time (offline-simulated online judge), checks no bin overflows, sums packed value. Floor 0 on any overflow. Normalize vs greedy "first bin that fits"

specs.title: Interactive Adaptive Probing (find hidden hotspots)
specs.objective: maximize total reward of discovered "hot" cells using ≤ `Q` probes on a hidden grid, where each probe returns a noisy local measurement guiding the next probe
specs.io: interactive: respond to probe results; final report = set of guessed hot cells
specs.innovation: **Bayesian/optimistic search: maintain a posterior heat estimate, probe the cell with the highest upper-confidence-bound (UCB), update a Gaussian-smoothed belief grid incrementally around the probe; spend the last few probes confirming top candidates** — the UCB-driven adaptive probe schedule is the innovation
specs.scoring: local judge holds a hidden hotspot map, answers probes (deterministic given seed), then scores Σ reward over reported hot cells minus penalty for false positives, using ≤ Q probes. Floor 0 if > Q probes or malformed report. Normalize vs uniform-grid probing

specs.title: Sokoban-Style Box Pushing (max boxes parked)
specs.objective: maximize the number of boxes pushed onto target cells within `S` moves by a single agent on a grid, classic push-only mechanics
specs.io: `H W S`, grid with walls/agent/boxes/targets → a move string in `{U,D,L,R}`
specs.innovation: **macro-move A\*/beam: precompute, per box, the push-reachable target set and the agent-repositioning cost; search over the order of "park box X on target Y" macros with a beam scored by boxes-parked and remaining-move budget, using a deadlock detector (corner/edge) to prune** — the macro-action abstraction + deadlock pruning is the lever over raw move search
specs.scoring: scorer replays the move string under exact push rules, counts boxes on targets at the end (or first time all parked), checks move budget. Floor 0 on an illegal move (into a wall / pushing a box into a wall). Normalize vs a greedy nearest-box-to-nearest-target pusher

specs.title: Conveyor / Belt Layout (route items by tile rotation)
specs.objective: maximize items delivered from sources to sinks by placing/rotating directional belt tiles on a grid, items advancing one tile per tick deterministically
specs.io: `H W`, sources, sinks, tile budget → a tile type+rotation per chosen cell
specs.innovation: **build belt paths as the union of shortest source→sink routes, then SA on tile orientations where the delta is measured by a single deterministic forward simulation restricted to the connected component the changed tile belongs to** (component-local resim) — localizing the simulation to the affected belt component is the efficiency innovation
specs.scoring: scorer lays the tiles, simulates item flow for a fixed horizon, counts delivered items, checks no two tiles overlap and budget respected. Floor 0 if a tile is on a source/sink illegally or budget exceeded. Normalize vs straight-line belts

specs.title: Watchman Route (max area seen, bounded steps)
specs.objective: maximize the number of distinct grid cells ever visible to a guard walking a closed route of ≤ `L` steps on a grid with walls (visibility = line-of-sight)
specs.io: `H W L`, grid, start → a move string forming a closed route
specs.innovation: **precompute each cell's visibility set (bitset) once; then the route is a budgeted orienteering where each step's marginal gain = popcount of newly-seen cells, optimized by a beam over (position, seen-bitset-summary) with a submodular upper bound for pruning** — the precomputed visibility bitsets + submodular bound make incremental coverage cheap
specs.scoring: scorer replays the route, unions visibility of every visited cell, counts distinct seen cells, checks route closed and ≤ L. Floor 0 if route open or over budget or walks into a wall. Normalize vs a boustrophedon sweep route

specs.title: Pipe/Tile Connection Puzzle (max connected pairs)
specs.objective: maximize the number of matching colored endpoints connected by non-crossing rectilinear paths on a grid (flow-free style), partial connections allowed
specs.io: `H W`, endpoint pairs with colors → for each connected pair, its path
specs.innovation: **route by hardest-pair-first (most-constrained) with A\* on a congestion-priced grid; when stuck, rip up and reorder by a learned difficulty score (length of forced detour), each cell tracking its owner color so conflict tests are O(1)** — most-constrained-first ordering with rip-up is the heuristic core
specs.scoring: scorer checks each claimed path connects same-color endpoints with unit steps and no cell shared; objective = #pairs connected. Floor 0 on a shared cell or invalid path. Normalize vs greedy shortest-path-per-pair (counting only conflict-free pairs)

specs.title: Knapsack-with-Synergies Selection
specs.objective: maximize Σ item values + Σ pairwise synergy bonuses of a selected item subset under a weight budget `W` (the pairwise term makes it non-separable / quadratic knapsack)
specs.io: `n W`, item weights & values, synergy pairs `i j bonus` → the chosen subset
specs.innovation: **start from the LP-relaxed (linearized) quadratic knapsack rounding, then a flip-based local search where adding/removing item `i` updates the objective in O(deg_synergy(i)) using per-item incident-synergy lists and a running weight total** — the incident-synergy incremental delta turns an O(n²) re-evaluation into O(degree)
specs.scoring: scorer sums selected values + synergy bonuses for pairs both selected, checks Σ weight ≤ W. Floor 0 if over budget. Normalize vs value/weight-ratio greedy (ignoring synergies)

specs.title: Time-Indexed Crew Rostering
specs.objective: maximize covered shifts minus overtime/penalty assigning `W` workers to a weekly grid of shifts, respecting rest rules (no back-to-back, max hours)
specs.io: `W D S`, shift demands & values, worker availabilities → a `W×D` assignment grid
specs.innovation: **column-generation-flavored construction (each worker's feasible weekly pattern is a "column"), pick patterns greedily by marginal coverage, then SA that swaps one worker's day-shift with an incremental rest-rule check confined to that worker's adjacent days** — the per-worker pattern abstraction + local rest-rule check is the lever
specs.scoring: scorer validates rest rules per worker and counts covered shift-value minus overtime penalties. Floor 0 if any rest rule violated. Normalize vs greedy fill-by-demand

specs.title: Reconfiguration Routing (move tokens to targets)
specs.objective: minimize total moves relocating `k` labeled tokens on a grid from start to target cells, tokens block each other, one token moves one step per action
specs.io: `H W k`, start positions, target positions, walls → a sequence of (token, direction) actions
specs.innovation: **prioritized planning (à la multi-agent path finding): order tokens by a difficulty score, plan each with space-time A\* avoiding the reserved space-time of higher-priority tokens; resolve deadlocks by a windowed re-plan, with reservations stored in a hash set for O(1) collision tests** — space-time reservation prioritized planning is the established non-obvious method
specs.scoring: scorer replays actions, checks no two tokens ever occupy a cell, all reach targets, reports total actions. Floor 0 if a collision or a token misses its target. Normalize vs sum of independent Manhattan distances (lower bound) / sequential one-at-a-time mover

specs.title: Adaptive Auction Bidding (online resource buy)
specs.objective: maximize total utility of resources won across `T` sequential auctions under a fixed budget, each round revealing one item's value and a price signal, bid decided before the next is shown
specs.io: interactive/streamed: budget, then per round `value price_hint` → a bid each round
specs.innovation: **adaptive bidding policy: maintain a budget-pacing multiplier (dual variable) updated by online mirror-descent so the average spend tracks budget/T; bid value·(1−pacing) and only when value-per-cost beats a running quantile of seen items** — the dual-variable budget pacing is the online heuristic-design innovation
specs.scoring: local scorer replays the round stream feeding the solver one item at a time (offline-simulated online judge), awards items where bid ≥ price, deducts price, checks budget never exceeded, sums won utility. Floor 0 on a budget breach. Normalize vs spend-evenly fixed-fraction bidding
